paper.title: Structural and Kinetic Characterization of the 4-Carboxy-2-hydroxymuconate Hydratase from the Gallate and Protocatechuate 4,5-Cleavage Pathways of Pseudomonas putida KT2440

identity_policy: Aliases below are local author-ledger labels, not proposed biological CURIEs or authority approvals. Parent must bind issuing identifiers and reconcile later chemistry evidence.
scope: Fresh full 2016 paper reading, all main sections, five tables, nine figures, six equation images; no maintained-file edit or approval verdict.

evidence.source_assertion: Figure 1A depicts gallate conversion by GalA to OMA, GalD-dependent tautomerization to CHM, GalB hydration to CHA, and GalC cleavage to oxaloacetate plus pyruvate.

claims.scope: Gallate branch only
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Figure 1A is a pathway summary; parent should ground all four steps in the 2005/2011 primary studies. It is not fresh evidence for every whole-pathway occurrence.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified GalA and His6-tagged GalD converted gallic acid in an oxygen-bubbled reaction to a mixture containing CHM; chromatography separated CHM, OMA and gallic acid.

claims.scope: Combined GalA/GalD preparation in vitro
claims.limitations_and_disposition: This supports the combined preparation and oxygenated context; do not assign a full individual catalytic stoichiometry from the combined assay alone.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: KT2440 GalD overexpressed in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography; His6 tag retained because the 361-residue protein contains an internal thrombin site at residue 239. Tag terminus is not specified here.

evidence.source_assertion: KT2440 GalD overexpressed in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography; His6 tag retained because the 361-residue protein contains an internal thrombin site at residue 239. Tag terminus is not specified here.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec6; #sec7; #sec8 paragraph on GalD and LigJ purification

quantitative_details.conditions: 150 mM gallic acid, 750 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0, repeated enzyme additions for 50 min and another 30 min incubation

evidence.source_assertion: GalB catalyzed CHM hydration to CHA and the reverse dehydration of CHA. Polarimetry showed production and consumption of the negative CHA enantiomer under the reported conditions.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec16; #sec25 paragraph following Table 3; Table 4 (#T4); Figure 5 (#F5)

claims.scope: Purified wild-type GalB; metal-reconstituted enzyme; individual assay host not explicitly assigned
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Maintain reaction reversibility and the negative optical sign. Absolute CHA configuration is unresolved by this study; source calls the GalD-derived CHM (2E,4E) using prior characterization.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

GalB hydrates CHM, the enol tautomer, rather than directly hydrating OMA. Without GalD, coupled reactions proceeded slowly at a rate independent of hydratase concentration, attributed to spontaneous OMA-to-CHM tautomerization.

claims.scope: Coupled in vitro reactions
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Do not infer that OMA can never contribute material: spontaneous tautomerization supplies CHM. Keep this conditional distinction local to the GalB hydration step.

evidence.source_assertion: Figure 1A assigns water to the GalB/LigJ hydration step converting CHM to CHA; the enzyme assays measure both CHM hydration and reverse CHA dehydration.

claims.scope: Hydration reaction
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Water is a reactant in the forward hydration, distinct from a metal cofactor. Issuing reaction authority must establish exact protonation and stoichiometry.

evidence.source_assertion: Co2+-reconstituted GalB converted CHM into a CHA product with negative optical rotation. In racemic CHA, GalB consumed the negative enantiomer and left positive optical rotation.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 Figure 5 (#F5); #sec16 final paragraph; #sec25 paragraph following Table 3

claims.scope: Optical rotation at 589 nm; 100 mM HEPES pH 7.5
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Negative rotation is not an R/S assignment. Figure 9 identifies S only as compatible with the proposed model.

evidence.source_assertion: The reconstructed gallate pathway couples GalA, GalD, GalB and GalC to oxaloacetate detection via malate dehydrogenase. Omission of GalB prevented the reported NADH oxidation.

claims.scope: Coupled in vitro pathway; observation marked data not shown
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Supports GalB requirement in this assay and transfer toward GalC. GalC reagent identity and purification are not separately documented in the 2016 methods; use 2011 for exact GalC claims.

evidence.source_assertion: GalB overexpressed in KT2442 and aerobically purified contained predominantly zinc among measured metals; zinc occupancy was about 23%, while cobalt and copper were about 0.1% and iron below 0.6%.

claims.scope: KT2440 gene product overexpressed in KT2442; ICP-MS and separate ferrozine assay
claims.limitations_and_disposition: The authors warn aerobic purification could lose iron, so this does not establish exclusive physiological zinc use. ICP-MS iron background was inadequate; iron bound uses ferrozine result.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: KT2440 galB subcloned into pVLT-31 and overexpressed in P. putida KT2442; protein purified aerobically through three chromatographic steps. This is native-host overexpression, not a measurement of undisturbed intracellular occupancy.

evidence.source_assertion: KT2440 galB subcloned into pVLT-31 and overexpressed in P. putida KT2442; protein purified aerobically through three chromatographic steps. This is native-host overexpression, not a measurement of undisturbed intracellular occupancy.
The active GalBNt truncation contained zinc in its crystal, coordinated by His14, Asp17, Glu48, His127 and water; fluorescence and anomalous diffraction supported zinc at the site.

claims.scope: GalBNt crystal; N-terminal four-residue deletion
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Structural zinc concerns the truncation construct. Figure 3C compares unrelated PIG-L proteins and does not establish their occurrence in this pathway.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: GalBNt lacks the first four N-terminal residues of GalB, was cloned into pT7-7 and expressed in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3). The crystal structure and its bound zinc concern this active truncation construct.

evidence.source_assertion: GalBNt lacks the first four N-terminal residues of GalB, was cloned into pT7-7 and expressed in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3). The crystal structure and its bound zinc concern this active truncation construct.

EDTA-treated GalB regained CHM hydratase activity after preincubation with Zn2+. With 50 micromolar Zn2+, Table 4 reports a CHM turnover of 2.08 per second and catalytic efficiency of 8.12e5 per molar per second.

claims.scope: In vitro apoenzyme reconstitution for at least 1 h; standard assay 25 C, HEPES pH 7.5
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Represent zinc as supported assay cofactor without claiming exclusive in vivo use.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.
Fe2+-reconstituted GalB hydrated CHM with the highest tested turnover. Fe2+ was introduced anaerobically; the measured catalytic efficiency differed by less than threefold from Co2+ and Zn2+.

claims.scope: In vitro apoenzyme reconstitution; 50 micromolar ferrous ammonium sulfate
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Higher turnover is conditional; physiological metal remains unresolved. Paper reports less than 3% activity loss after 1 h air exposure following anaerobic loading.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

Co2+-reconstituted GalB hydrated CHM with higher turnover than Zn2+-reconstituted enzyme; the catalytic efficiencies differed by less than threefold because substrate affinity also changed.

claims.scope: In vitro apoenzyme reconstitution for at least 1 h; 50 micromolar CoCl2
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Co2+ is an effective alternative assay cofactor, not established as the physiological metal.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.
EDTA treatment reduced Zn2+-saturated GalB activity, with half-lives of 32.3 min at 250 micromolar EDTA and 17.1 min at 1 mM EDTA. After 12 h in 1 mM EDTA, activity was below assay error.

claims.scope: Purified GalB under specified chelation conditions
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Prefer condition in catalysis/cofactor description. If represented as an inhibition edge, EDTA acts through metal removal and must not imply a cellular regulator or universal zero activity.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified KT2440 GalB, reported as wild type. The study describes expression in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3) and KT2442, but does not assign every kinetic batch to one host. GalB tag status is not explicit. Metal reconstitution is stated on the edge.
Table 2 reports residual activity of 4.0% for apoGalB and 0.030% with EDTA relative to Fe2+-reconstituted enzyme. These assay rows should be retained alongside the long-incubation chelation result.

claims.scope: Distinct assay conditions
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Do not rewrite the paper as apoGalB having absolutely no activity under all conditions, and do not reinterpret the residual as evidence of metal-independent catalysis.

evidence.source_assertion: The tested metal panel gave lower activity with Mn2+, Fe3+, Ni2+, Ca2+, Mg2+ and Cd2+ than with Fe2+ or Co2+; Cu2+ gave very low activity under the same panel conditions.

claims.scope: 50 micromolar CHM, 50 micromolar added metal, HEPES pH 7.0
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Retain the complete panel as conditional biochemical context. Do not infer all tested ions are physiological cofactors, or infer copper regulation from relative activity alone.

evidence.source_assertion: Adding 50 micromolar Co2+ increased the activity of GalB purified from KT2442 about fourfold. The authors attribute this to incomplete metal loading during overexpression or loss during purification.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec25 paragraph 1; Table 2 caption and Native rows (#T2)

claims.scope: Native-host overexpressed, aerobically purified material
claims.limitations_and_disposition: This is reconstitution of an underoccupied preparation, not evidence of cobalt-mediated transcriptional regulation.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: KT2440 galB subcloned into pVLT-31 and overexpressed in P. putida KT2442; protein purified aerobically through three chromatographic steps. This is native-host overexpression, not a measurement of undisturbed intracellular occupancy.

evidence.source_assertion: KT2440 galB subcloned into pVLT-31 and overexpressed in P. putida KT2442; protein purified aerobically through three chromatographic steps. This is native-host overexpression, not a measurement of undisturbed intracellular occupancy.
Purified GalB bound Zn2+ and Co2+ with submicromolar dissociation constants; H127A weakened binding much more than E48A. The H14A/D17A variant could not be saturated up to 500 micromolar metal.

claims.scope: PAR binding assay after metal reconstitution
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Affinity and mutagenesis support cofactor binding; do not assert that E48 is unimportant to catalysis because its metal-binding effect is smaller.

evidence.source_assertion: The GalBNt crystal forms a D3 hexamer, and GalB gel filtration gave about 156.2 kDa, consistent with the predicted hexamer mass of 164.8 kDa.

claims.scope: Crystallographic truncation plus solution GalB gel filtration
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Paper reports gel-filtration data not shown. Do not mint a GalB complex CURIE; use a verified native complex if the parent obtains one. The two asymmetric-unit protomers are not the proposed biological dimer.

evidence.source_assertion: The GalB construct lacking its first four N-terminal residues retained the reported CHM activity of wild-type GalB and was used for the solved crystal structure.

claims.scope: GalBNt in E. coli
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Same activity is a reported comparison, not a full published kinetic parameter set for the truncation. Keep its structural claims separate from full-length constructs.

evidence.source_assertion: The paper demonstrates matching negative CHA optical products for GalB and LigJCsE6, but does not establish the absolute configuration of that product; S-CHA appears only as the model-compatible assignment.

claims.scope: GalB and Comamonas E6 LigJ preparations
claims.limitations_and_disposition: No exact S-CHA endpoint may be grounded solely on this paper. It also does not equate LigJ proteins across bacterial strains or establish KT2440 uses the full protocatechuate pathway.

evidence.source_assertion: Both GalB and LigJCsE6 utilized CHM produced by GalD. The discussion attributes its (2E,4E) identity to the 2011 NMR interpretation and challenges an earlier (2Z,4E) assignment in a LigI crystal.

claims.scope: Fresh enzyme-substitution comparison with historically assigned substrate
claims.limitations_and_disposition: 2016 does not report a new direct NMR assignment of all substrate geometries. Preserve later-source conflicts rather than transferring one historical label to every CHM authority identifier.

evidence.source_assertion: Replacing GalB by Comamonas E6 LigJ in the coupled gallate assay gave NADH oxidation stoichiometric with input gallate; omitting GalD made the reaction slow and hydratase-concentration independent.

claims.scope: Reconstituted gallate assay with heterologous replacement
claims.limitations_and_disposition: This is assay complementation, not natural whole gallate pathway occurrence in Comamonas E6 or identity of GalB and LigJ.

endpoint_qualifiers_proposed.description: Codon-optimized Comamonas sp. E6 pmdE (GenBank BAI50711.1) expressed from pET28a in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3); N-terminal His6 tag removed with thrombin, followed by removal of tag and uncleaved protein.

evidence.source_assertion: Codon-optimized Comamonas sp. E6 pmdE (GenBank BAI50711.1) expressed from pET28a in E. coli BL21(lambdaDE3); N-terminal His6 tag removed with thrombin, followed by removal of tag and uncleaved protein.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec6; #sec7; #sec8 paragraph on GalD and LigJ purification

evidence.source_assertion: GalB catalyzed reversible interconversion of CHPD and HMG, with much lower catalytic efficiency than CHM hydration; only negative HMG was consumed from the racemic mixture in polarimetry.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec12; #sec16; Table 4 (#T4); Figure 5 (#F5); #sec25 paragraph following Table 3

claims.scope: In vitro side-substrate assays
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Retain as enzyme side activity outside the exact gallate-to-pyruvate/oxaloacetate route. The DDVA-to-HMG pathway proposed in Figure 1B is not thereby established physiologically.

evidence.source_assertion: Neither wild-type GalB nor its A16D variant was inhibited by glucosamine or N-acetylglucosamine at concentrations up to 1 mM in the reported CHM hydration assay.

claims.scope: Specified in vitro assay and two constructs
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Retain as a conditional negative. Do not add a positive inhibition edge or assert absence of inhibition in all conditions.

evidence.source_assertion: The abstract reports that the A16D variant lacked detectable hydrolase activity, while its CHM catalytic efficiency fell about 9.5e4-fold; Table 4 shows that A16D was not saturated by CHM up to 2 mM.

claims.scope: A16D engineered variant
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Main methods do not provide a separately detailed hydrolase substrate panel or detection limit. Preserve that limited reporting instead of a broad absence-of-function claim.

evidence.source_assertion: E48A greatly reduced CHM catalytic efficiency and shifted a free-enzyme pH transition; H164A lowered turnover with little change in CHM affinity and shifted another pH transition.

claims.scope: Separate engineered variants, Zn2+ assays
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Supports proposed proton-transfer roles, not direct observation of each proton path. Preserve variants if adding experimental construct edges; do not convert residues into free participants.

evidence.source_assertion: The authors propose that Glu48 activates metal-bound water for addition at CHM C4 and His164 protonates C5, followed by tautomerization and protonation at C3. This is a model supported by kinetics and mutagenesis.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 Figure 4B (#F4); Figure 9 (#F9); #sec31 paragraphs on proposed mechanism

claims.scope: Proposed catalysis, not ligand-bound structural observation
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Substrate/product co-crystallization, soaking and computational docking did not yield a catalytically productive experimental structure or model. Do not make the modeled S-CHA an established product identity.

evidence.source_assertion: Arg21, Arg67 and Arg216 substitutions impaired CHM use. R216A strongly reduced CHM efficiency but affected CHPD efficiency less, supporting a proposed interaction with the CHM carboxylate absent from CHPD.
evidence.source_locator: PMC4817193 #sec27 paragraph 2; Table 4 (#T4); #sec31 modeled binding paragraph

claims.scope: Separate R21A, R67A and R216A constructs
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Residue assignments are mechanistic interpretation, not direct substrate-bound electron density.

evidence.source_assertion: Y123A retained near-wild-type CHM turnover, whereas the engineered A16D change strongly impaired hydration. The results support a GalB mechanism distinct from the related PIG-L deacetylases.

claims.scope: Y123A and A16D mutant assays
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Do not label Y123A completely neutral: its Table 4 efficiency is lower than wild type, despite the authors describing no significant change in utilization.

evidence.source_assertion: CHM absorbance changes supported an enol pKa near 7.3, and Zn2+- and Co2+-GalB had similar pH-profile shapes. Kinetic parameters were limited to the tested pH range because substrate affinity became unfavorable outside it.

claims.scope: In vitro titration and kinetic models over pH 5.5-9.5
claims.limitations_and_disposition: The pH data support an enolate substrate interpretation. They do not establish a cellular pH optimum or pathway regulation. Figure 6 caption swaps B/C relative to actual axis labels; cite axes explicitly.

evidence.source_assertion: MultiGeneBlast identified clusters with GalB or LigJ homologs in several bacterial groups. Figure 8 presents a small sample of these computational hits and their neighboring homologs.

claims.scope: Computational homology and neighborhood
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Do not promote these taxa as experimentally confirmed complete gallate degraders or infer biochemical identity of all homologs. Figure labels and species taxonomy require separate authority checking.

evidence.source_assertion: The discussion recounts earlier rescue of a ligJ-deficient Sphingomonas derivative by GalB on vanillate or syringate, using previous studies as evidence for related CHM substrate use.

claims.scope: Secondary discussion of earlier experiments
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Parent must inspect original experiments for a new rescue edge; do not cite the 2016 narrative as a newly performed experiment, nor infer a complete KT2440 protocatechuate pathway.

evidence.source_assertion: Figure 1B proposes a route linking biphenyl-derived CHPD through hydratases and HMG aldolase to pyruvate. The paper separates this proposal from the established gallate branch in Figure 1A.

claims.scope: Adjacent proposed pathway
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Keep DDVA, HO-DDVA, LigX/LigZ/LigY and the proposed CHPD-to-HMG physiological route outside a narrow gallate degradation I record unless independently scoped as an interface.

evidence.source_assertion: The 2016 methods specify GalB and GalD expression and purification, including a retained His6 tag on GalD, but give no GalB protein accession and no separate GalC reagent preparation for the coupled assay.

claims.scope: Bounded identity assessment of this paper only
claims.limitations_and_disposition: Use the inspected 2011 construct table and issuing authorities to establish GalB/GalD/GalC accession bindings. Lack of a reported GalB tag does not prove an unmodified native N- or C-terminus.
